correctness.rationale: Theorem reconstructs a finite height-at-most-two poset transfer with each upper coordinate subtracting t_b times its largest lower-neighbour coordinate, t_b in [0,1]. The image inequalities (1-t_b)y_a <= y_b <=1-t_by_a for each a<b yield a convex bijective target and the stated inverse. On a unique-max chamber its Jacobian splits orthogonally into triangular weighted star blocks; eigenvalues of S^TS outside the identity space solve z^2-(2+U)z+1=0. The largest possible squared star weight is W=max_a sum_{b>a}t_b^2; a strictly interior order-polytope point can force every upper neighbour of a maximizing a to choose it, giving infinitesimal equality for both map and inverse. Convexity and finite piecewise-affine decomposition give global bounds, including zero weights and disconnected graphs. Independent NumPy singular-value check and source-reviewed checker.py corroborate but do not prove the universal theorem.
